chapter_title: The Explanation of the Peace, what it is; the Right Hand; the Kiss; the Salutation.
chapter_note: The first half preserves a coherent cosmological teaching: five ritual “signs” are primordial mysteries enacted in the descent/ascent drama of the First Man (cosmos→cosmos). From ¶10 onward the same items are repeatedly re-applied to human custom “in the midst of mankind” and then to church initiation and hierarchy (cosmos→contemporary practice), with strong second-half pastoral/application drift (editorial fatigue). A probable scriptural/Christianized enthronement formula appears inside ¶14, embedded in an otherwise cosmological sequence.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Dialogue/Q formula (“disciples… questioned the apostle”) functions as compiling frame; sets up topic rather than expounding cosmic mechanics.

paragraphs.core_text: So, these five signs are the mystery of the First Man. He came forth with them from the aeon of light. Also, when he finished his contest, he went up with these good signs. They received him into the aeons of light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution (“Then he says to his disciples”) and the cosmos→world application setup (“displayed in the world as miniatures… I am the one who can reveal…”), which shifts from describing what the mysteries ARE to asserting present instruction.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core teaching begins when the five signs are identified as intrinsic to the First Man’s descent/ascent (system-internal). The preceding sentences are an editorial/teaching-presentation bridge to ‘the world’ and to the speaker’s authority.

paragraphs.core_text: The first peace is the one that the gods and the angels in the land of light gave to the First Man; when he comes out against the enemy. The gods and the angels were walking with him; escorting him, giving to him their peace and power, and their blessing and fortification. This is the first peace that the gods and the angels gave to the First Man; as he comes forth from the aeon of light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic mythic explication (cosmic agents, land of light, descent against the enemy) without institutional/ethical application.

paragraphs.core_text: The first right hand is the one that the Mother of Life gave to the First Man; when he comes out to the contest.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Tight cosmological identification: divine being → act toward First Man; no reach into human society.

paragraphs.core_text: The first kiss is this one with which the Mother of Life embraced the First Man; as he separates from her, coming down to the contest. Even all the gods and the angels who are in the aeons of light were making to embrace him! [ ... ] all of them also, and the church tutelaries (?), and the kinsfolk who belong to the household of his people. They were making to embrace him as [he] separates from them, accompanying him out, embracing him with the kiss of affection and love.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic household scene (aeons of light; gods/angels; kin of the household). The language stays within the heavenly community rather than mapping onto contemporary rites.

paragraphs.core_text: The first salutation is the salutation with which the First Man made obeisance; when he comes out [to the depths] below. He was bending his knees, making obeisance to the God of truth, and all the aeons [of light] who belong to the household of his people; entreating them for a power to escort him, as he comes forth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic liturgy/action narrated as part of descent-myth; no “today/in the midst of mankind” hook.

paragraphs.core_text: The first laying on of hands is the one that the Mother of Life bequeathed upon the head of the First Man. She armed him and made him mighty. She laid hands on him, and sent him to the battle. He descended. He completed his struggle with the great powers and the enmity.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic arming/empowerment within the contest narrative; despite elevated rhetoric, it remains cosmological.

paragraphs.core_text: By the [se] five signs and these five myst[e]ri[es] the First Man came forth from the aeons of light against the enemy. He humbled him. He was victorious against him by them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary of fivefold structure as operative mechanics in the cosmic struggle (degree/number pattern).

paragraphs.core_text: Also, when he ascended from the war, he came in to the kingdom of the household of his people by these five mysteries!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the descent/ascent arc within the aeons; no institutional extension.

paragraphs.core_text: The peace with which [he ascen]ded is the peace that the summons gave to him, [w]hen it was sent forth from the [Fa]ther of Life. It gave him the peace in the world of darkness. Also, that peace with which he descended is th[e sam]e as the one with which he ascended from the struggle!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the concluding application to contemporary practice (“Therefore… this peace here and now… among the powers of the Father”), which pivots from cosmic description to justification of present ritual peace.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens with system-internal soteriology (Summons/Father of Life; world of darkness). The turn to “here and now” signals later application.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, this second right hand is the one that the Living Spirit gave the First Man, when he [brou]ght him upward out from the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ‘appropriate to the mystery… occurs in the midst of mankind’ extension, which maps the cosmic act directly onto human custom.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Clear seam from cosmological rescue (Living Spirit) to human handshake ritual.

paragraphs.core_text: Also, this second kiss is the one with which the [Father o]f Life and the Mother of the living embraced the First Man, when he ascended from the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the explanation of the kiss’s use among mankind (travel/homecoming scenarios), a cosmos→social-life mapping.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic embrace is core; the ethnographic/social application is editorial.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] second salutation with which the First Man made obeisance [ ... this] time to the God of truth and [ ... ] the blessed aeons and al[l] the aeons [ ... the] whole [land] of light, whe[n] the Father of Life and the Mother of the living brought the Man upward from the abyss of the struggle.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the sentence applying the salutation to what occurs “today in the midst of mankind”.
paragraphs.temporal_note: System-internal reprise of obeisance within the ascent drama; the ‘today’ marker is a late anchoring to contemporary behavior.

paragraphs.core_text: The second laying on of hands is this: When the Living Spirit brought the First Man upward from the war, he saved him from all the surging waves. He brought him upward, he gave him ease in the great aeons of light, which belong to the household of his people. He set [him] firmly before the Father, the Lord of the totality. Now, when he went up before the great Father of the lights, a voice came forth to him from the heights, saying: [ ... ] He received this great laying on of hands that he may become leader of his brethren in the new aeon.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed (1) the enthronement/‘right hand… footstool’ quotation, likely a scriptural/Christianized insertion into the mythic scene; and (2) the closing cosmos→mankind application (“Again, appropriate to the mystery… occurs in the midst of mankind… authority to the lesser”).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying narrative (Living Spirit’s rescue; presentation before the Father; leadership in the new aeon) is cosmological. The embedded enthronement formula is strongly biblicizing in diction, and the final ‘in the midst of mankind’ is editorial application.
Explicit historical legitimation (“proclaimed… by an apostle”) and explanation of institution in this world: hagiographic/compiling voice rather than the impersonal substrate.
Cosmic being (Light Mind) is used to ground church formation (“choose his church”): cosmos→institution mapping, characteristic of later ecclesial application.
Initiation order and community categories (“child of peace”, election to the faith, approach the church) are operational church teaching, not system-internal cosmology.
Explicit obeisance to the holy church and moral program (“good works”)—institutional/ethical overlay.
Church-building language (charity; conformed/built up) with ritual sequence applied to communal life; no cosmological mechanics being expounded.

paragraphs.core_text: At the time of their coming forth, the Light Form shall come forth before them; and she redeems them from the darkness to the light [ ... ] This Light Form calms the person, with the kiss and her quiet, from fear of the demons w[ho de]stroy his body. By her asp[ec]t and her image [the] heart of the elect one, who is come forth from his bo[d]y, shall be calm for [him]. Afterwards, the angel who h[o]lds the victory prize extends to him the right hand. And it draws him out of the abyss of his body, and accepts him in with the [k]iss and love. That soul shall make obeisance to its red[eem]er, who is this Light Form. And also, at the inst[ant when ... ] he shall be perfected and increased according to [ ... / ... ] in the household of the living ones, with the go[ds] and the angel[s] [An]d he receives the crown [ ... ] glory in the life for ever.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the opening discourse marker “Once again:” and the closing institutional list (“and all the apostles and the chosen”), which reads as a community-facing addition appended to an otherwise cosmological eschatology.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is an internal eschatological choreography (Light Form; angel with victory prize; right hand/kiss as cosmic actions). The tail-end institutional cataloging suggests later community redaction.
Direct exhortation and address (“my brethren and my limbs… let you…”) anchors to audience practice; not substrate exposition.
Second-person encouragement/exhortation about understanding the rites; fragmentary but clearly audience-directed application.
Explicit church hierarchy (teachers, deacons, presbyters) and command to honor offices: institutional discipline layer.
Second-person pastoral exhortation (“my beloved ones…”) with practical/moral assurances; the cosmological substrate is no longer being expounded.
